summary.title: Scenario A - Cedar Grove Volunteer Portal

threats.title: A02 Hijacked account can modify records
threats.description: An attacker obtains a staff member's credentials through credential leakage, password reuse, or brute-force attacks and successfully authenticates to the Cedar Grove Portal as that staff member. Because staff accounts are authorized to review requests, update household records, and assign deliveries, the attacker can make unauthorized changes to household information and delivery assignments, which affects the integrity of client records and operations.
threats.mitigation:
PROPOSED: Enforce the use of MFA for staff accounts. This reduces the chance of account theft as the attackers will need access to the MFA, which can still be possible by stealing their login token but it's harder to take effect. 
OWNER: Coordinator. 
CHECK: Create a test account with the regular accesses for staff accounts with MFA enforced. Try to authenticate using only the username and password without providing the second factor. Verify that access is denied until successful MFA verification is completed.

threats.title: A05 Volunteers actions cannot be traced
threats.description: Volunteers use a shared dispatch login to access the Cedar Grove Portal and download weekly delivery lists. Since multiple volunteers use the same account, the organization cannot determine which volunteer accessed or downloaded a specific CSV file. If delivery information is accessed inappropriately, a volunteer can deny responsibility because all activity appears under the same shared account.
threats.mitigation:
PROPOSED: Replace the shared dispatch account with individual volunteer accounts and maintain access logs showing the account, timestamp, and downloaded files. 
OWNER: Coordinator 
CHECK: Create separate volunteer accounts and verify that downloads by different volunteers are recorded under their own identities in the audit logs.

threats.title: A03 Disabled Volunteer keeps access to downloaded files
threats.description: Volunteers can download weekly delivery lists as CSV files to personal phones or other devices. Even if a volunteer's portal or shared-folder access is removed later, copies of previously downloaded CSV files may remain on their personal devices. A former volunteer could intentionally or accidentally disclose household names, addresses, contact details, and delivery information to unauthorized individuals, resulting in exposure of client information.
threats.mitigation:
PROPOSED: Reduce distribution of downloadable CSV files by providing read-only access where possible. If exported delivery lists must be shared, distribute them through controlled services such as Microsoft OneDrive, SharePoint, Google Drive, or a managed shared folder with access controls. Limit downloads to users who require offline access and remove access when volunteers leave the organization.
OWNER: Coordinator
CHECK: Create a test volunteer account, download a delivery list, then disable the account and verify that the user can no longer access newly shared delivery lists. Confirm that access to shared resources is revoked and that distribution mechanisms enforce the intended access restrictions.

data.name: D1 Household Database
data.description: This database stores household names, addresses, contact details, delivery requests and confidential intake notes.

threats.title: A04 Database outage prevents portal operations
threats.description: The Cedar Grove Portal relies on a hosted database to store and retrieve household records, delivery requests, intake notes, and delivery assignments. If the database becomes unavailable due to a denial-of-service attack, infrastructure failure, or service outage at the hosting provider, staff and volunteers may be unable to access or update records. This could delay delivery scheduling and disrupt services for households that depend on the organization.
threats.mitigation:
PROPOSED: Deploy a highly available database architecture with a standby replica or failover database instance. Monitor database availability and establish backup and recovery procedures so that the portal can continue operating or be restored quickly in the event of an outage.
OWNER: Coordinator
CHECK: Simulate a database outage by disabling the primary database or database connection. Verify that the secondary database or failover process becomes active and that staff can continue viewing and updating records through the portal with minimal interruption.

threats.title: A01 Email Service threat impersonating a client
threats.description: The Cedar Grove Portal accepts delivery requests through a public web form. The scenario does not describe any client authentication or account verification process. An attacker could submit requests while pretending to be an existing client by providing their name, address, and contact information. This could result in fraudulent requests, incorrect household records, or misuse of delivery resources.
threats.mitigation:
PROPOSED: Require clients to create accounts protected by a username, password, and multi-factor authentication before submitting or modifying requests. Additionally, verify ownership of the registered email address before activating new client accounts.
OWNER: Coordinator
CHECK: Create a test client account and attempt to submit or modify requests using only publicly known information about that client. Verify that requests cannot be submitted or changed without successful authentication and MFA verification.
